messages:
maria: Heads-up: customer ACME (private VPC) reporting inference flakiness after we pushed runtime update yesterday — NCCL timeouts + CUDA illegal instruction on some nodes. Logs attached.

jonathan: can you paste the nvidia-smi and driver/kernel versions from affected hosts?

maria: here's snippet:
```shell
nvidia-smi
Driver Version: 510.54
CUDA Version: 11.6
Kernel: 5.15.0-70-generic
```

kai: 510 driver + 5.15 should be ok generally, but some of our on-prem images expect 520+ for the new kernels we shipped. Are they on our validated matrix?

maria: customer is stable on paper, but they did manual driver update last month to 515 (vendor supplied). I see drift to 510 on some nodes — mixed driver versions in the same cluster.

ashley: mixed driver versions cause NCCL init mismatches — we should never have heterogeneous driver across a single ring. Recommend cordon/replace nodes.

jonathan: can we add an onboarding check that verifies full 'supported matrix' (driver/kernel/nccl/cuda)? We currently validate model runtime but not host drivers for Private.

maria: customer refuses full rolling upgrade—they want minimal downtime. They claim our supported matrix only lists 'tested' but not 'required' levels.

kai: that's the dispute — private installs interpret the matrix as permissive. We need clearer required minima. Also need automated drift detection + report flag to support.

ashley: from infra ops POV, short term: orchestrate an in-place driver reconcile: upgrade all nodes to 520. If vendor image blocks, fallback to guarded pool with 515-compatible runtime. I'll draft runbook.

support-bot: Incident created: #INC-2025-327 — customer ACME: onprem-driver-drift. Assigned to @ashley and @kai.

maria: adding logs from one failing pod:
```log
NCCL WARN When using ibVerbs, csq failed: rdma_connect error
CudaError: illegal instruction
```

jonathan: looks like kernel ABI mismatch too. Which kernel modules are loaded? `modinfo nvidia` output?

maria: `modinfo` shows tainted modules from vendor-supplied nvidia-legacy. We'll need coordinated vendor driver swap.

kai: long term: add a 'host-agent' in Private that reports driver/kernel/cuda and can auto-install supported drivers or recommend steps. Also, update our matrix doc to state 'required' vs 'tested' explicitly.

ashley: agreed. I'll open a docs PR and schedule a customer-facing call to propose a low-downtime plan. Who can lead the upgrade windows? @kai?

kai: I can own the upgrade window next Tue 03:00 UTC. Will prepare a canary and rollback plan.

maria: thanks. for ticket: customer requested a compatibility waiver while they validate. We should log waiver duration and risk.

jonathan: added: create automated alert if heterogeneous driver versions detected in the same ring; severity P2.

ashley: quick note about cost: if we move ACME to a guarded 515 pool it reduces throughput and increases per-token GPU cost. Sales should set customer expectations.

maria: pinging @sales-lead to coordinate. end.
